_comment: Single source of truth for all discipline rules. Edit here — scorer, guardrails and reports all read this file. Times are IST wall-clock minutes (e.g. 810 = 13:30).
_sizeCap_comment: FIXED 2026-07-28 (Anoop): was 6, silently 3x looser than the documented hard rule (CLAUDE.md rule #2: max 2 contracts/entry). The 150K eval breach on 2026-07-21 was exactly this — sized 5 lots, doubled to 10, against a stated 2-cap the app was never actually enforcing at this number. 2026-08-15: these BASE numbers are now the FUNDED ruleset — stageRules.eval permits upward from here, stageRules.funded clamps. See stage-rules.js for why the safe numbers are the base ones.
_sizeFloor_comment: ADDED 2026-08-15. One-contract trades lose money in BOTH stages — eval 25% win rate/-$361 over 12 trades, funded 54% win rate but still -$345 over 13 trades, because the wins are too small to pay for the losses. Sizing down to 1 is not caution, it is what hesitation looks like in the ledger. 2 contracts is the only size profitable in both stages (eval +$535, funded +$264), and it survives dropping its single best trade in both.
_tradeLimit_comment: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28 by tradesPerSession/tradesPerDay below — kept only so any code path still reading the old shape doesn't crash. Do not raise this back up as the active limit.
_tradesPerDay_comment: CHANGED 2026-08-15: was 10. The base rules are NORMAL (non-scalper) mode, and Anoop's own note sets normal mode at under 5 trades/day. Scalper raises it to 10 via scalperRules; funded clamps it to 6 via stageRules. Trade COUNT is owned by the tradingMode axis — stageRules.eval deliberately does not set it, so switching to eval can never raise the count above what the mode allows.
_maxHoldSeconds_comment: ADDED 2026-08-15. Normal-mode ceiling of 30 min; scalperRules tightens to 900 (15 min). Anoop's note put a 15-min MINIMUM on normal mode; the data says the opposite — trades held over 15 min are 40% win rate and -$646 net across 15 trades, while the 5-15 min window is 22% of his trades and 145% of his profit (+$1,975, robust to dropping its best trade). Caveat kept on record: hold time is an outcome, not a decision, and those long holds are most likely failed scalps he refused to cut rather than planned swing trades — so this is a ceiling on hanging on, not evidence that swing trading fails for him.
_qualifying_comment: 2026-07-28 (Anoop): only trades that closed with |P&L| >= $100 count toward the 5/session, 10/day cap. Anything that closed between -$100 and +$100 is a scratch/near-breakeven trade and doesn't count as one of the 5.
_payout_comment: ADDED 2026-08-23. REPLACES eval.consistencyPctMax, which was 50 — a number matching NO published Tradeify tier, and which grep showed was read by no code anywhere in the repo. The consistency rule is the hard gate on the entire goal of this app (reach a payout), and it was both mis-specified and untracked. Figures below are from Tradeify's own help centre: https://help.tradeify.co/en/articles/10468320-rules-consistency-rule (limits) and /11083796 (Growth day counts). Read by payout-eligibility.js. Per this repo's convention, no consistency figure may be hardcoded in code or in a persona string — it lives here.

payout._accountFamily_comment: ⚠ UNCONFIRMED — inferred, needs Anoop to verify against his Tradeify dashboard. The live broker account reads TDFYSL50413184562; the TDFY+SL prefix reads as Tradeify SELECT. If that is wrong, change this one value — everything else follows from it. Do NOT let an inferred tier silently become fact; that is exactly how the wrong 50 got here.
payout._profitField_comment: The firm writes 'no single day's profit (commissions are not included in profit)', which reads as evaluating GROSS. Defaulting to net ('pnl') is deliberately conservative: net is smaller, so the computed ratio is HIGHER and the app calls him ineligible slightly BEFORE the firm does, never after. Switch to 'gross' only once a real payout request settles the ambiguity.

selectEval.label: Select Evaluation
selectEval._comment: 40% during the evaluation phase. The 3-day minimum is a consequence of the rule, not a separate gate: no single day may exceed 40% of total, so it cannot be passed in 1-2 days.

selectFunded.label: Select Funded
selectFunded._comment: Tradeify publishes NO consistency rule for Select once funded. null means 'no limit configured' — payout-eligibility.js treats that as not-computable rather than as automatically satisfied.

growthFunded.label: Growth Sim Funded
growthFunded._comment: 35%, plus 5+ days each showing profit above a size-dependent floor ($100 on 25k, $150 on 50k, $200 on 100k, $250 on 150k). 250 matches eval.start of 150000 above — re-check this if the account size changes. The day count resets after each successful payout.

lightningFunded.label: Lightning Funded
lightningFunded._comment: Accounts bought after 2025-09-12 08:00 EST scale 20% → 25% → 30% by payout number; earlier accounts stay at 20% flat. Only the first-payout figure is encoded here — if this family ever becomes active, the scaling must be implemented rather than left at 20.

scalperRules._comment: Override rules when tradingMode === 'scalper'. Anything NOT listed here falls through to the standard rules above. 2026-08-15: sizeCap deliberately REMOVED from this block — contract size is now owned by stageRules (eval/funded), not by trading style. Leaving it here meant switching to scalper mode on a FUNDED account silently raised the size cap, which is the exact change his own data says destroys that account (funded: every size except 2 contracts loses money, -$1,717 across 31 trades).
scalperRules._tradesPerDay_comment: CHANGED 2026-08-15: was 15 (session 8). Anoop's note: scalper may exceed 5 trades, up to 10/day.
scalperRules._maxHoldSeconds_comment: CHANGED 2026-08-15: was 1800 (30 min). Anoop's note says scalper hold time is under 15 min, and the data agrees — over 15 min is 40% win rate, -$646 across 15 trades.

stageRules._comment: ADDED 2026-08-15. The eval/funded risk layer, applied AFTER scalperRules — see stage-rules.js for the full derivation and the fail-safe argument. Anoop's strategy, verbatim: 'I want to risk aggressively in evaluation and be very secure when I'm creating a funded account, safe in funded... Spend less time in evaluation, more time in funded.' eval PERMITS upward from the base; funded CLAMPS and can only ever tighten (same one-way-ratchet idea as lossRatchet.mode 'min'). Trade COUNT is intentionally absent from the eval block so that being in eval can never raise the count above what the trading mode allows.

eval._comment: Size 2-4. His 3-4c bucket is +$2,007 over 14 trades and stays +$1,286 after dropping its best trade, median +$57 — a real edge. 5-6c is NOT kept: +$506 that collapses to +$24 once one +$482 trade is removed, i.e. one lucky trade rather than an edge. This is where I disagreed with his handwritten note, which said scalper size 4-6 max 6; he accepted the cap of 4 on 2026-08-15. contractsPerDayMax 36 is deliberately near-non-binding: all six of his eval days above 12 contracts were GREEN (+$2,865, 6/6), and an intraday daily-loss stop COSTS money in eval at every level tested. The eval constraint is meant to be the clock, not the size.

funded._comment: Fixed at 2 contracts — not a range. 2c is the largest funded sample (20 trades) and the only profitable one (+$264, still +$83 after dropping its best trade, median +$8). Every other size loses: 1c -$345, 3c -$437, 4c -$103, 5-6c -$384, 7c+ -$449, totalling -$1,717 over 31 trades. contractsPerDayMax 12 = 6 trades x 2c, confirmed by the day-level data: all three funded days above 12 contracts lost (-$1,763, 0/3 green) while the two profitable funded days ran 10 and 11 contracts. dailyLossCap 200 comes from an intraday simulation walking each day's trades in order and halting at the cap — every level helps in funded and tighter is monotonically better ($200 -> +$795, $300 -> +$583, $500 -> +$219). It matches the dayStop.funded of 200 already in this file, which was never actually enforced.

_lossRatchet_comment: ADDED 2026-08-12 (Anoop's own rule): tomorrow's maximum loss may never exceed what he made today. Targets his stated failure mode - 'after a couple of profit days, one day eats all my profits'. mode 'min' = cap is min(normal dayStop, yesterday's profit) - it can only ever TIGHTEN. This matters: the rule as first described ('max loss = yesterday's profit') would set an $800 cap after an $800 green day, i.e. 4x the $200 rule, loosening risk exactly after the good days that historically precede a blow-up. mode 'raw' would allow that; do not use it. floor = the cap never drops below this, so a tiny green day ($20) doesn't make tomorrow untradeable. A red or flat yesterday leaves the normal dayStop in force. warnAtPct = show a caution banner at this percentage of the cap.
_requireChecklist_comment: ADDED 2026-08-12 (task #33). Until now the pre-trade checklist was advisory - nothing stopped a trade without it. On 2026-08-10 Anoop skipped it and lost $855.50, and named it himself afterwards as the thing he was supposed to do. It is now a HARD NO-GO reason, ranked with the daily stop, not a soft 'pending' one (soft renders as amber PENDING CHECK-IN, which is precisely the ignorable state that let this slide for months). Set false to disable - deliberately a config switch rather than something he has to delete code to bypass, because guards that cannot be turned off get ripped out instead.
_contractsPerDay_comment: ADDED 2026-08-12. Caps TOTAL contracts traded per day, which nothing did before: sizeCap limits each ENTRY to 2, and tradesPerDay limits COUNT to 10 - but ten legal 2-lot trades is twenty contracts, every one inside the rules, day already lost. max=12 comes from Anoop's own five logged days, which split on exactly this: 10c=+$440, 11c=+$157.50, 12c=-$142, 24c=-$879.50, 29c=-$572.50. Under ~12 he makes money or loses small; past 24 he loses a week. Same trader, same setups - only the size changed. 12 contracts = six 2-lot trades, which also lands near the 3-4 trades/day profile of evaluation PASSERS in his own research file (failures average 6.8; his logged average is 6.4).
_biasAdherence_comment: ADDED 2026-08-13 (Anoop, verbatim): 'I should follow the trade direction according to it. 70% to 80% should be in the same direction.' targetPct 75 is the midpoint of the range he named; warnPct 60 is where Jessi starts naming it rather than just reporting it. DIRECTION OF RECORD = the Daily Bias field from the pre-trade checklist (his call 2026-08-13); 4H and 1H are logged as CONTEXT and downgrade confidence when they disagree, they do not override or veto. This became computable only on 2026-08-13: before that the checklist record stored {date, score, tier} and threw the bias/h4/h1 away, so there was nothing to compare trades against. minTradesToJudge stops a 1-trade day reading as '0% adherence' - one counter-trend scratch is not a pattern. Set enabled:false to silence the whole feature.
_f3_comment: LIVE_FEED_LOOP_PLAN 5.3 (F3 inverted R:R): fire when realized avgLoss >= f3Ratio x avgWin with >= f3MinWins confirmed wins and >=1 confirmed loss today. His documented ratio is ~15.6:1; 2 is a deliberately early warning (MISTAKE_PATTERNS_PLAN.md F3). Advisory only.
_signalJoin_comment: LIVE_FEED_LOOP_PLAN 5.1: a closed trade joins back to the nearest preceding armed signal on the same instrument and direction within this many minutes (measured to trade entry).
_autoPostSessionReview_comment: ADDED 2026-08-12 (Anoop): the full Post-Session Analyst report used to auto-fire 5s after EVERY CSV upload, on top of the auto-debrief - two AI calls per upload. The report is ~5-7K tokens in and ~1.5K out (roughly $0.014 on Haiku), and Anoop's words: 'it is such a long list of details... I cannot read the whole post-session review every time I upload a CSV'. Generating something unread is 100% waste at any price. Now OFF by default: the short debrief still fires on upload, and the full report runs only when explicitly asked - 'End Day & Save', or typing 'post session review' in chat. Set true to restore the old auto-fire behaviour.
